title: Space Rogue
build: Origin Systems' two-sided disk, G64 images of side 1 (SHA-256 f8f4bdd5…) and side 2 (944b0898…) from the C64 Preservation Project's collection (orientation.md)

records.c: Log-addition correction, 1,280 entries for a difference d of two logs below 5.0 (index d, page $A5 plus d's whole part): 256 * log2(1 + 2^(-d/256)) less 1, from $FF down to $0A. log_add_mag adds it, plus one, to the larger log. MAIN's base entry at $A49A calls SEG1 at addresses inside it (s_A54E and the others): at a base SEG1 is loaded here instead
Byte 78 of the log-addition table in flight; at a base SEG1's routine called from $A4CE
Byte 93 of the log-addition table in flight; at a base SEG1's routine called from $A4AA
Byte 117 of the log-addition table in flight; at a base SEG1's routine called from $A4CB
Byte 132 of the log-addition table in flight; at a base SEG1's routine called from $A4D1
Byte 371 of the log-addition table in flight; at a base SEG1's flag that ends the base loop at $A4DF when nonzero
Byte 372 of the log-addition table in flight; at a base SEG1's routine the base loop calls each pass ($A4E2)
log_add_table from difference 2.0: the base address in log_add_mag's ADC at $B3C6, whose high byte (at $B3C8) is set to $A5-$A9 by the difference's whole part
The log-addition table's last page, differences 4.0 to 4.996: corrections $15 down to $0A

Log-subtraction correction for differences d of 1.0 to 4.996 (page $A9 plus d's whole part): -256 * log2(1 - 2^(-d/256)) less 1, from $FF down to $0B; log_sub_mag subtracts it, and one more, from the larger log
log_sub_table from difference 2.0: the base address in the SBC at $B339, its high byte patched at $B33B
Byte $187 of log_sub_table in flight; at a base SEG1's status page, called from $26A8 (Navigation's STATUS loads SEG1 to show it)
Low bytes of the log-subtraction correction for differences below 1.0, where the result can fall far below both numbers; high bytes at $AF00 (difference $6B and up uses 1)
High bytes for log_sub_near_lo, differences 0 to $6A: $14 at 0 (the two cancel, leaving a log of about -20, zero), falling to 2
Low bytes of 2^(i/256) * $4000 for the fraction i of a log, 256 entries; high bytes at $B06B. log_to_lin shifts this mantissa by the whole part
High bytes of 2^(i/256) * $4000: $40 to $7F
256 * log2(1 + i/256) for i = 0-255: the fraction of a log for the 8 significant bits of a number; lin_to_log adds the whole part
Log subtraction, d of 5.0 (the whole part 5): 6 to 12 taken off the result's log, more for a smaller low byte of d; one of the pieces at $B26B-$B2C8 that $B2C9 picks by d's whole part
Log subtraction, d of 9.0: one off the log when d's low byte is below $88, nothing otherwise
Log subtraction, d of 8.0 (and of 7.0 with a low byte of $F3 or more): one off the log
Log subtraction, d of 7.0: 3 or 2 off the log
Log subtraction, d of 6.0: 6 to 3 off the log
Adds the negative correction in A to the result's log

Log subtraction when the logs differ by 5.0 or more: the result is the larger number, with the whole part of d kept in the operand at $B2D5 to pick the small correction (5 to 9); 10 or more needs none
The operand of LDA # at $B2D4: $B2C9 writes the difference's whole part here, and the CMPs that follow pick its correction
Log subtraction of magnitudes with no sign test, entered by MAIN's unused arcsine ($98C2): d = ($5F) - ($62), then on as at $B36B
Log subtraction when the second magnitude is the larger: the sign in $61 is flipped and the result is (second - first), by the same tables
The high byte of the SBC operand at $B339: $B32D writes $A9 plus the difference's whole part, the page of log_sub_table
Log subtraction, d of 1.0 to 4.996: the log less the log_sub_table entry (page from d's whole part, kept in the operand at $B353) and one
The high byte of the SBC operand at $B351: $B345 writes $A9 plus the difference's whole part
Subtracts the log-form number in $62-$64 from the one in $5F-$61, result in $5F-$61: opposite signs add the magnitudes (log_add_mag), the same sign subtracts them ($B361)

log(|a| - |b|) with a's sign, or b - a with the sign flipped when |b| is the larger ($B2F8); differences below 1.0 use the 16-bit table at $AE00/$AF00, larger ones log_sub_table or the small corrections
Adds the log-form number in $62-$64 to the one in $5F-$61, result in $5F-$61: the same sign adds the magnitudes (log_add_mag), opposite signs subtract them (log_sub_mag)

log(|a| + |b|): the larger log plus a correction for the difference d of the two (swapped first when $62/$63 is the larger): from log_add_table below 5.0 (its page kept in the operand at $B3C8), from steps of 11 down to 0 for 5.0 to 9.5, none above; the sign byte $61 is left alone
The operand of LDX # at $B3B8: log_add_mag writes the swapped difference's low byte here, the index into log_add_table
The high byte of the ADC operand at $B3C6: log_add_mag writes $A5 plus the difference's whole part, the page of log_add_table
Log addition, d of 5.0 or more: adds the correction to the result's log, given in A as 256 less it and patched into the operand at $B411
The operand of SBC # at $B410: written with 256 less the correction log_add_mag adds for differences of 5.0 and up
The signed byte in A, as a whole number, to log form: sign-extended into $60/$61 with $5F zero, then byte_to_log's tail ($B447)
The signed 16-bit whole number in $60/$61 ($5F is set to zero) to log form, negated first when negative; the sign stays in $61
The unsigned 16-bit whole number in $60/$61 ($5F set to zero) to log form

The signed 24-bit number in $5F-$61 (16.8 fixed point) to log form in $5F/$60, the sign left in $61: the top nonzero byte gives the whole part from $B545 and a shift count from $B4C5 (patched into the branch at $B49E) that brings 8 significant bits down to index log_table
The offset of the BNE at $B49E: lin_to_log writes the shift count's branch offset from log_shift_table here
For lin_to_log, by the top nonzero byte's value: the branch offset into the shift code at $B4A1-$B4BD that leaves its 8 significant bits in X
For lin_to_log, by the top nonzero byte's value: the whole part of its log2 plus 8 ($08 for 1 to $0F for $80-$FF), added to $F0 or $F8 when the number is below $10000; $FC for zero
log_to_lin, then the 24-bit result negated when the sign byte $61 has bit 7 set

The log-form number in $5F/$60 to a positive 24-bit number in $5F-$61 (16.8 fixed point): the mantissa from exp_table_lo/hi by the fraction, shifted by the whole part through the branch offset from $B671 patched into $B5F5; a whole part of 15 or more saturates to $7FFFFF, a very negative one gives 0 or 1
The offset of the BNE at $B5F4: log_to_lin writes the branch offset from exp_shift_table here, 0 (fall through to saturate) for an overflow
log_to_lin's results for the smallest logs: 0, or 1 at $B605, or the mantissa shifted down 6 at $B609, written as a 24-bit number
log_to_lin's case for a whole part of 14: the mantissa moved up a byte
For log_to_lin, by the whole part of the log (a signed byte): the branch offset into its shift code ($B601-$B670); 0 for 15 to 127, an overflow; $0B for the most negative, a result of zero
Clamps the signed 16-bit number in $60/$61 to a signed byte in A: $7F above 127, $80 below -128, else $60
Fills the TAC panel of the $C000 bitmap (character rows 18-23, columns 14-23, less its top and bottom pixel rows) with the byte in $3B, and its screen colours at $E2DE with $CC
Copies the TAC panel from the $C000 bitmap and its colours ($E2DE) to the same places in the $4000 bitmap and its screen at $6000, so both display buffers show it
Clears the 3D view of the $C000 bitmap (character rows 3-15, columns 4-35) to the byte in $3B and its screen colours at $E07C to $CC
Clears the 3D view of the $4000 bitmap (character rows 3-15, columns 4-35) to the byte in $3B and its colours at $607C to $CC
Zeros to the end of SEG0
STA: the Starbase's model (type $13), 475 bytes, loaded at $E400 by load_model. Its prologue, relocated there, points $7A/$7B at its header and jumps to draw_model

STA's header, copied to $9A-$BD: prepared, so its reference points and normals are filled in (first byte 1); 18 points, 4 reference points, 14 normals, 14 polygons, 8 axis vectors; then 15 pointers to its tables
STA's size, 475 bytes, by which load_model moves the heap pointer on
STA's 4 reference points, as point numbers (4, 8, 9, 17): each normal is tested from one of them
STA's 8 axis vectors, 9 bytes each (three log-form components: fraction, whole part, sign); the points are built by adding and subtracting them, and preparation adds the scale to their logs
Byte 55 of STA's axis vectors in flight; at a base, SEG1A's routine that MAIN calls at $A4D4 when the player docks
For each of STA's 18 points, the point it is built from, negative for the model's own position
For each of STA's points, the axis vector added to its parent, negative to subtract it
STA's reference points in its own frame, 9 bytes each, linear and negated, filled in when it is prepared
STA's 14 face normals, 9 bytes each in log form, each made when the model is prepared as the cross product of two edges of a polygon
For each of STA's normals, which reference point its facing is tested from
For each of STA's 14 polygons, the normal whose facing decides its pass in the painter's order: 0 the middle pass, negative reversing the test
For each of STA's polygons, its own normal, which says whether its front or back is seen
For each of STA's polygons, the colour code its back is drawn in, $FF for not drawn
For each of STA's polygons, the colour code its front is drawn in (set_colour), $FF for not drawn
The number of vertices of each of STA's polygons (48 in all)
STA's polygons' vertices, as point numbers, one polygon after another

STA's face groups, the normals of each group in turn: when the player touches the model, facing_face finds the first group all turned toward the player; group 0 is a base's docking face, any other is a collision
The number of normals in each of STA's 3 face groups (6, 5, 5), ended by a zero
ICR: the Cruiser's model (type 3), 379 bytes, loaded at $E5DB by load_model. Its prologue, relocated there, points $7A/$7B at its header and jumps to draw_model

ICR's header, copied to $9A-$BD: not yet drawn, so its reference points and normals are still zero (first byte 0); 18 points, 3 reference points, 8 normals, 11 polygons, 9 axis vectors; then 15 pointers to its tables
ICR's size, 379 bytes, by which load_model moves the heap pointer on
ICR's 3 reference points, as point numbers (6, 8, 11): each normal is tested from one of them
ICR's 9 axis vectors, 9 bytes each (three log-form components: fraction, whole part, sign); the points are built by adding and subtracting them, and preparation adds the scale to their logs
For each of ICR's 18 points, the point it is built from, negative for the model's own position
For each of ICR's points, the axis vector added to its parent, negative to subtract it
ICR's reference points in its own frame, 9 bytes each, linear and negated, filled in when it is prepared
ICR's 8 face normals, 9 bytes each in log form, each made when the model is prepared as the cross product of two edges of a polygon
For each of ICR's normals, which reference point its facing is tested from
For each of ICR's 11 polygons, the normal whose facing decides its pass in the painter's order: 0 the middle pass, negative reversing the test
For each of ICR's polygons, its own normal, which says whether its front or back is seen
For each of ICR's polygons, the colour code its back is drawn in, $FF for not drawn
For each of ICR's polygons, the colour code its front is drawn in (set_colour), $FF for not drawn
The number of vertices of each of ICR's polygons (40 in all)
ICR's polygons' vertices, as point numbers, one polygon after another

ICR's face groups, the normals of each group in turn: when the player touches the model, facing_face finds the first group all turned toward the player; group 0 is a base's docking face, any other is a collision
The number of normals in each of ICR's 1 face group (6), ended by a zero

INIT's entry, called once from SR ($14E2) with the carry set for an old game: a new game copies the 12-byte name from $BF00 to $0711. Zero page $38-$FF is cleared and MAIN, SPB, EXTERN and FONT are loaded ($EA3E). An old game then loads SAVED to $0403, asks for side 2, loads SEG0, restores the ship (copy_ship_stats, load_slot_models); a new one asks for side 2, loads SEG0 and sets up the first sector (start_game_objects, load_nav_tiles, load_system_map, enter_sector). Both redraw ($A14C), restore after the disk (restore_after_disk), turn the engine hum on and set the view ($65B0)

Death, from $1B93: the hum off, the screen cleared ($EA23), and a message for what killed the player by the type in $0835 (a missile, a ship type, an object or a hazard: disk texts $CF67-$CF6E, or $CEAF less the value when it is negative) and $CF6F; after a key it asks for side 1, loads TITLE to $2000 and starts it again. A base overwrites this code ($E400-$EAFF is SEG1A there); END is loaded on leaving to put it back
A negative $0835 picks disk text $CEAF less its complement
Clears the bitmap at $C000-$DFFF and sets the border black (set_border)

Loads MAIN to $6400, SPB to $BD00, EXTERN to $EB00 and FONT to $F200, then sets up the display: $0D03 = 1, the bitmap cleared, bitmap and multicolour modes on, $D018 = $80 (screen $E000, bitmap $C000), bank 3 shown ($8EF6), black border and background, the colour RAM white; then $A164, $87FE and window 0 ($9E4C)
Zeros to the end of INIT
